script.text: Iran says its missiles now have no range limit. Who is in reach?

A Revolutionary Guard spokesman said Saturday that Iran's old limit on missile range has been lifted for the Guard. The cap was two thousand kilometers. He did not say whether Iran has longer-range missiles.

The Associated Press notes Iran is not known to have such missiles. U.S. officials warn its space technology could be adapted. The spokesman linked the move to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's warning of a response without geographic limits.

Meanwhile, Trump says U.S. forces hit an Iranian air defense system in new limited strikes. He called them minor. Iranian media report explosions on Qeshm Island. Iran is also reviewing Qatari proposals aimed at bridging gaps with Washington. The U.S. says its naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.
Will Iran and the U.S. agree to a deal before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran Drops Its Missile Range Limit. What Does It Mean? #shorts
upload.description:
On Saturday, November 7, a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the Guard's self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range, about 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles), has been lifted. The spokesman said the restriction "has been lifted for us" and tied it to a warning from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei that any threat from the United States or Israel would be met with a response without geographic limits. He did not say whether Iran has missiles that exceed the old limit; according to the Associated Press, Iran is not known to have any, though U.S. officials have said technology from its space program could be repurposed for long-range missiles. Separately, President Donald Trump said U.S. forces carried out new limited strikes on an Iranian air defense system, which he called minor. Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and at the port of Jask; Iranian officials did not confirm strikes there. Iran is also reviewing Qatari proposals meant to bridge differences with the United States, according to AP. The U.S. says its naval blockade of Iranian ports continues. Most details come from officials and the parties themselves and could not be independently verified.
